title: Eastern Carolina vinegar sauce
summary: A thin, sharp vinegar and pepper sauce for chopped or pulled pork, with no tomato at all.
steps: Shake everything together in a jar until the salt and erythritol dissolve.
Refrigerate at least overnight so the pepper flakes flavour the vinegar.
Shake again and sprinkle over pulled pork (see the internal-temperature note in your pork recipe: 93–96 °C / 200–205 °F for pulling), tossing as you go. Serve more at the table.
Keeps for months in the fridge.
tips: Start with about 1/2 cup per 1 kg of pulled pork and add more to taste; the meat soaks it up.
Many cooks add no sweetener at all; the tablespoon of erythritol only rounds off the edge.

origin.history: Eastern North Carolina barbecue means whole hog, chopped and dressed with vinegar seasoned with red and black pepper. Vinegar-and-pepper dressings for pork are generally considered the oldest strand of Carolina barbecue, in use well before tomato-based sauces appeared, though no single starting date is documented. The region's cooks are known for keeping tomato out entirely, unlike the Piedmont (Lexington) style to the west.
